theory.intro: Because $1\text{ kg} = 1000\text{ g}$, a mass given in kilograms and grams can be written as a single decimal number of kilograms.
facts: $1\text{ kg} = 1000\text{ g}$, so $1\text{ g} = \tfrac{1}{1000}\text{ kg} = 0.001\text{ kg}$.
$3\text{ kg } 250\text{ g} = 3.25\text{ kg}$ — the grams become the decimal part.
steps: Keep the whole kilograms before the decimal point.
Divide the grams by $1000$ to get the decimal part.

foundation.question_text: Write $4\text{ kg }500\text{ g}$ as a decimal number of kilograms.
Write $2\text{ kg }250\text{ g}$ as a decimal number of kilograms.
Write $6\text{ kg }75\text{ g}$ as a decimal number of kilograms.
Write $3.6\text{ kg}$ as kilograms and grams.
Write $8.04\text{ kg}$ as kilograms and grams.

development.question_text: A parcel has a mass of $7\text{ kg }8\text{ g}$. Record its mass in kilograms using three decimal places.
A scale displays $5.305\text{ kg}$. State the mass in kilograms and grams.
Which is heavier: $2\text{ kg }90\text{ g}$ or $2.9\text{ kg}$?
development.solution_text:
$2\text{ kg }90\text{ g}=2.090\text{ kg}$
$2.090\text{ kg}<2.9\text{ kg}$
Therefore $2.9\text{ kg}$ is heavier.

development.question_text: Complete the equivalence: $9\text{ kg }\square\text{ g}=9.47\text{ kg}$.
A bag is labelled $3.016\text{ kg}$. What does the digit $1$ represent in grams?
development.solution_text:
$0.01\text{ kg}=10\text{ g}$
The digit $1$ represents $10\text{ g}$.

development.question_text: Order these masses from lightest to heaviest: $1\text{ kg }450\text{ g}$, $1.405\text{ kg}$, $1\text{ kg }54\text{ g}$.
development.solution_text:
$1\text{ kg }450\text{ g}=1.450\text{ kg}$
$1\text{ kg }54\text{ g}=1.054\text{ kg}$
$1.054<1.405<1.450$
The order is $1\text{ kg }54\text{ g}$, $1.405\text{ kg}$, $1\text{ kg }450\text{ g}$.

mastery.question_text: A digital scale rounds to the nearest $0.001\text{ kg}$ and shows $4.086\text{ kg}$. Write this as kilograms and grams.
Mia says $6\text{ kg }7\text{ g}=6.7\text{ kg}$. Correct her statement and explain the place-value error.
mastery.solution_text:
$7\text{ g}=0.007\text{ kg}$
$6\text{ kg}+0.007\text{ kg}$
$=6.007\text{ kg}$
Mia treated grams as tenths instead of thousandths of a kilogram.

mastery.question_text: A mass is written as $12.08\text{ kg}$. A second label shows $12\text{ kg }800\text{ g}$. Are the labels equivalent? Explain.
mastery.solution_text:
$0.08\text{ kg}=80\text{ g}$
$12.08\text{ kg}=12\text{ kg }80\text{ g}$
The labels are not equivalent.
